html:
Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has been president of Djibouti since 1999, after serving for two decades as chief of staff and security chief to Hassan Gouled Aptidon.

He has won repeated elections, most boycotted by the opposition, and the constitution was changed to let him run again. His rule has been built on the country's position on the Bab el Mandeb strait.

He leased land to the United States at Camp Lemonnier after 2001, and later to China, Japan, Italy and others, and invited Chinese money to build ports, free trade zones and a new railway. In 2018 his government took the Doraleh container terminal from Dubai's DP World. Djibouti has stayed calm in a troubled region, but power stays in one family.
